title: Meeting Action Item Detection with Regularized Context Modeling
research_question: Can regularized modeling of both nearby and non-contiguous meeting context, together with lightweight reuse of different pretrained models, improve sentence-level action-item detection across Chinese and English meetings?
methodology: The authors formulate action-item detection as binary sentence classification and release AMC-A, a manually annotated Chinese corpus containing 424 meetings, 306,846 utterances, and 1,506 action items, alongside experiments on 101 action-item-labeled AMI meetings. AMC-A candidate sentences are preselected using temporal expressions and action-related verbs, independently annotated by three annotators with contextual information, and adjudicated by an expert when labels disagree. Context-Drop supplies local context from adjacent sentences and global context retrieved by n-gram cosine similarity, randomly or deterministically drops context during training, and adds a bidirectional KL-divergence consistency loss; experiments report positive-class F1 over five runs. A lightweight model ensemble is also tested by combining the encoder layers of one pretrained model with the pooler of another without increasing inference-time model size.

key_findings.finding: AMC-A substantially expands publicly described action-item resources in the study, containing 424 meetings, 306,846 utterances, and 1,506 labeled actions, with train/dev/test splits of 295, 65, and 64 meetings.
key_findings.section: 2.2 Building A Large-scale Chinese Meeting Corpus

key_findings.finding: Action-item annotation remained subjective despite detailed guidelines: average pairwise kappa among AMC-A annotators was 0.47, followed by expert review of disagreements.
key_findings.section: 2.2 Building A Large-scale Chinese Meeting Corpus

key_findings.finding: Adding ordinary local and global context already improved AMC-A StructBERT positive F1 from 67.84 for the focus sentence alone to 69.09 for local plus global context.
On AMC-A, dynamic Context-Drop with local and global context achieved 70.82 positive F1, an absolute gain of 2.98 over the sentence-only baseline and 2.10 over the corresponding R-Drop configuration.

On AMI, the strongest reported Context-Drop configuration was fixed Context-Drop with local context at F1 43.12, compared with 38.67 for sentence-only StructBERT and 42.72 for local-context R-Drop; the configuration that was best on AMC-A was therefore not universally best.
Removing the KL-divergence regularization term degraded Context-Drop configurations on both corpora, supporting the claim that the gain is not explained solely by context-dropping data augmentation.

The lightweight hybridization experiment provided modest gains without an additional inference model: a StructBERT encoder with a RoBERTa pooler reached 68.36 F1 versus 67.84 for StructBERT alone, while the reverse hybrid improved RoBERTa from 66.87 to 67.25.

limitations: AMC-A annotation candidates are prefiltered using temporal expressions and action-related verbs, which can bias the labeled set toward explicit action formulations and potentially miss implicit actions.
Average pairwise kappa of 0.47 indicates substantial annotation subjectivity even after guideline development.
AMI labels are indirect: dialogue acts linked to action-related abstractive summaries are treated as positive rather than being directly annotated as action items.
AMC-A is Chinese and biased toward work meetings, while much of AMI is scenario-based, so cross-domain and cross-language generalization remains only partially tested.
Global context is retrieved with relatively simple n-gram cosine similarity rather than learned discourse or semantic retrieval.
The task is binary sentence detection and does not directly output normalized action object, owner, deadline, condition, commitment/request type, or supporting evidence spans.
The lightweight ensemble gains are small and were evaluated separately from the strongest Context-Drop setup.
The study evaluates manual transcripts rather than presenting an end-to-end ASR-to-action extraction evaluation.
raw_claims: The paper releases the Chinese AliMeeting-Action Corpus with manual action-item annotations.
AMC-A sentences containing action-item information such as task description, timeframe, or owner are positive examples.
Three annotators independently label candidate sentences while viewing their context.
Average pairwise kappa on AMC-A is 0.47.
The AMI benchmark is derived indirectly from dialogue acts linked to action-related abstractive summaries.
Local context is adjacent to the focus sentence, whereas global context is relevant but non-contiguous.
Dynamic Context-Drop reached positive F1 70.82 on AMC-A with local and global context.
Fixed Context-Drop with local context reached F1 43.12 on AMI.
Removing the KL consistency loss reduced Context-Drop performance.
The paper provides links to both the released corpus and action-item-detection code.
